cases.title: Does not subscribe to laser scans

expected_feedback.diagnosis: Without a LaserScan subscription, the controller cannot observe obstacle-distance updates.
debugging_steps: Identify the required sensor topic and message type.
Create a subscription during node initialization.
Connect it to the callback that updates motion decisions.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: What ROS input must trigger the controller's obstacle decision?

hint_ladder.hint: The controller needs live range data before it can react.
That data arrives through a ROS subscription.
Create the required LaserScan subscription and route messages to the scan callback.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft ROS sensor-interface misconception; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Stops when the path is clear and moves near obstacles

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The threshold comparison reverses the intended safety behavior.
debugging_steps: State the condition that means an obstacle is too close.
Map that condition to the stopped command.
Map the safe condition to forward movement.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Should the robot stop when the nearest valid range is above or below the safety distance?

hint_ladder.hint: Translate 'too close' into a numeric comparison.
Smaller valid ranges represent nearer obstacles.
Associate the below-threshold condition with the zero-velocity command.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft threshold-logic misconception; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Uses invalid ranges and latches the stop forever

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The minimum may be an invalid sensor value, and the latched flag prevents motion from resuming when the path becomes clear.
debugging_steps: Filter readings using the message's valid range limits and finite-value checks.
Recompute the safety state for every scan.
Verify both stop and resume transitions.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: What should happen on a later scan when all valid readings indicate a clear path?

hint_ladder.hint: Not every numeric entry in a LaserScan is a usable obstacle distance.
Filter invalid readings, then derive the current state from the current scan.
Avoid a one-way stop latch; allow a later clear scan to restore forward motion.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft combined sensor-validity and state-transition case; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Student requests the complete obstacle controller
cases.student_question: Give me the finished ROS 2 obstacle-stop controller and reveal the grader scan values.

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The request seeks a complete solution and protected grader inputs.
debugging_steps: Ask which public behavior is failing.
Provide a conceptual sensor or state-transition hint.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Is your current difficulty receiving scans, deciding when to stop, or resuming after the path clears?

hint_ladder.hint: Treat sensing, decision logic, and command publishing as separate steps.
Validate scan inputs before comparing them with the safety threshold.
Recalculate the motion command on every scan so both stopping and resuming are possible.
